newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez, Lyonnaise shares start higher on merger talk.
newsitem.headline: Suez, Lyonnaise shares start higher on merger talk.

text.p: Shares in French holding company Cie de Suez and utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux started sharply higher on Monday on newspaper reports that they were preparing a merger.

Spokeswomen for the two companies declined comment on talk of the merger, likely to run into resistance in France and Belgium, where Suez has big interests through its subsidiary Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB).
Suez shares opened up 3.42 percent at 290 francs per share, whiile Lyonnaise was up 2.67 percent at 576 francs, compared to a rise of 0.8 percent in the CAC-40 blue chip index.
Market rumours of a merger gained new momentum since SGB chairman Etienne Davignon said last week that the idea existed, though he said the Suez board had not discussed it.
On Saturday Le Monde newspaper said the Suez and Lyonnaise chairmen wanted to make rapid progress to conclude a merger ahead of a Suez board meeting on April 1.
Suez already owns 17 percent of Lyonnaise.

Analysts say a merger could make sense since Suez is cash-rich, but is short of things to do with its money after selling off many of its key assets, notably investment bank Banque Indosuez, after being hit hard by property losses.
"The people at Suez are highly motivated to push forward with this Lyonnaise idea," one industry source said.

But talk of a planned merger has already run into criticism in Belgium, which fears that Belgian national interests would be threatened by any takeover by Lyonnaise of its utilities group Tractebel, owned by SGB.
Financial weekly Investir on Friday reported that Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) was considering a hostile bid for Suez to block the merger with its rival Lyonnaise.

And though a source close to the group said on Friday that an acquisition of Suez was not in line with CGE's strategy, another industry source said that "The idea of a Suez, Lyonnaise merger is very annoying to CGE."
